faq.q: What should I do when someone grabs?
faq.a: Let go, take a breath, and use words: Please stop grabbing. Can we take turns? If it keeps happening, ask a grown-up to help.
asks: What if someone grabs my toy?

faq.a: Take turns, use a timer, split things into equal parts, or play with it together. Fair means everyone gets a go.
asks: Tell me about the First Priya

faq.q: Do I have to share everything?
faq.a: No. Special things, like a new birthday present or your toothbrush, can be just yours. It is okay to put special things away before friends come over.
asks: Do I have to share my special toy?

faq.a: Because wanting something is a strong feeling, and waiting is hard for everyone, even adults. It gets easier the more you practise.
asks: Why don't I want to share?

faq.a: First-then means one person goes first, then the other has a turn. Saying it out loud helps everyone know their turn is coming.
asks: Tell me about the Then Leo

facts: A 2008 study in the journal Nature found that by about age 7 or 8, most children prefer to share things equally.
Taking a slow, deep breath helps the body calm down by slowing the heartbeat.

quiz.say: Leo and Priya both want the red crayon. Which is a fair idea?

options.show: Priya uses it first, then Leo

quiz.why: Taking turns means both of them get to use it.

wrong.0: Hiding it means only Leo gets it.
wrong.2: If it breaks, nobody gets it.

quiz.say: What helped Leo calm down before he talked?
quiz.why: A slow breath calms the body so you can think.

wrong.2: Grabbing harder makes the fight worse.
